key_insight: C-ReD provides a comprehensive, realistic Chinese benchmark for detecting AI-generated text by combining real-world prompts with outputs from multiple LLMs, reducing dataset homogeneity and improving detection generalization.
problem_solved: Addresses the shortage of diverse, realistic Chinese corpora for AI-text detection—previous datasets suffer from limited model variety and prompt realism, which weakens detector robustness in real-world scenarios.
method: Collect real-world Chinese prompts from diverse online sources and user scenarios.
Generate outputs using a variety of LLMs and curate human vs. AI labels with quality controls and metadata (model source, prompt type, length).
Release standardized benchmark splits and baseline detectors to evaluate cross-model and cross-prompt generalization.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a realistic evaluation bed for building and stress-testing Chinese AI-text detectors, improving robustness against real-world misuse like phishing and academic dishonesty.
visual_elements: Dataset composition chart (sources, LLMs, human vs. AI proportions)
End-to-end pipeline diagram: prompt collection → LLM generation → annotation → benchmark release
Benchmark results bar chart comparing baseline detectors across model sources and prompt types
Cross-model generalization heatmap or confusion matrix highlighting detection transfer failures
paper_title: C-ReD: A Comprehensive Chinese Benchmark for AI-Generated Text Detection Derived from Real-World Prompts
paper_authors: Chenxi Qing, Junxi Wu, Zheng Liu, Yixiang Qiu, Hongyao Yu
